note: Every constant the engine uses that is not measured. Returned by the get_assumptions tool so that even an assumption has a traceable source. The UI labels these as assumptions, not measurements.

water_in_orbit.source: Avoided launch cost. SpaceX published Falcon 9 price of about 2700 USD per kg to low Earth orbit, so a ton of water already in orbit displaces that much launch mass.

platinum_group_metals.source: Platinum at roughly 1000 USD per troy ounce

propellant_usd_per_ton.source: Industrial argon, the propellant Starlink thrusters use, at roughly 5 USD per kg

operations_usd_per_day.source: Order of magnitude for a small mission operations team, ground network time included

delta_v_split.description: NHATS publishes one total round trip delta v. The engine splits it evenly between the outbound leg and the return leg.
delta_v_split.confidence: simplification, a real mission would not split evenly

included_stay_days.description: The NHATS query that built the dataset required a stay of at least 8 days, so that much surface time is already inside round_trip_days. Mining beyond 8 days extends the mission.

ore_density_t_per_m3.source: Typical rubble pile bulk density, used only to check that a tonnage target is small next to the object

composition_model.description: Mass fractions by spectral class, with platinum group metals in parts per million. Each asteroid record carries a composition_source field saying whether its class came from published taxonomy, from an albedo inference, or from nothing at all.

sources.metallic_M: Iron meteorite bulk composition, roughly 89 percent iron and 8 percent nickel, platinum group metals at tens of ppm
sources.carbonaceous_C_and_B: CI and CM chondrite water content, 8 to 12 percent by mass as hydrated minerals
sources.stony_S: Ordinary chondrite composition, metal in the low tens of percent and essentially no water

composition_model.confidence: class assignment is often an inference, the fractions inside a class are literature averages
